deep.reconstruction:
WHAT IS COMPUTED. Put t_k = 80^k/(k!)^2. Every number on the page is a term of the series F(x) = Σ_k x^k/(k!)^2 = I_0(2√x) at x = 80, or a term k·t_k of x F'(x) = Σ k x^k/(k!)^2 = √x I_1(2√x). The terms are split by parity of k.

THE FOUR COLUMNS.
- Column 1 holds the even terms k = 2,4,…,26: 1600, 71111.1111, 505679.0123, 1031997.9844, 815450.5615 (k=10), 299522.7039, 57871.7942, 6430.1994, 439.5027, 17.5314 (k=20), .5257, .0110, .0002. The k = 0 term 1 is not written. Partial sum 2425839.6693; then 2790121.4009; final 2790121.9378.
- Column 3 holds the odd terms k = 1,3,…,25: 80, 14222.2222, 227555.5556, 825598.3875, 1019259.2685 (k=9), 539140.8671, 141785.8959, 20576.6379, 1779.9860, 87.6571 (k=19), 3.1803, .0795, .0014. Partial sum 2625856.3009; then 2790089.6581; final 2790089.7390.
- Column 2 holds k·t_k for odd k: 80, 42666.6667 (3t3), 1137777.7778, 5779188.7125, 9173315.4167, 5930549.5380, 1843216.6456, 308649.5691, 30259.7617, 1665.4840, 66.7863, 1.8284, .0353, .0005. Partial sum 22063578.1117; then 24247436.3584; final 24247438.2206.
- Column 4 holds k·t_k for even k: 3200, 284444.4444, 3034074.0741, 8255983.8750, 8154505.6148 (boxed), 3594272.4473, 810205.1090, 102883.1897, 7911.0488, 350.6282, 11.5647, .2650, .0043. Partial sum 23326480.4556; then 24247842.0060; final 24247842.2753. Below it are 438 and 403, apparently a start on the difference of the two weighted sums (≈ 404.05).

HOW THE TERMS ARE MADE. The scratch multiplications in the lower half show the method. Gauss steps through k = 1,2,3,… using two recurrences:
- t_k = t_{k-1}·80/k²;
- k·t_k = 80·t_{k-1}/k.
The divisions are done as small factors. Examples:
- 1779.98598097 ×4/9/2/9 → 43.950271135, i.e. t18 = 439.5027.
- 81545056148 ×8 = 652360449184; ÷11 → 5930549.538 = 11 t11; ÷11 → 539140.867 = t11.
- t11/3 = 179713.62; ×2 → 3594272.447 = 12 t12; ÷12 → t12.
- t13/2/7 ×8 → 810205.12 = 14 t14; ÷14 → t14.
- t16/2/17 ×16 → 30259.76 = 17 t17.
- 4t21 = 12.721204; ÷11 → 1.156473, i.e. 22 t22 = 11.5647 and t22 = .5257.

WHAT THE SUMS YIELD.
- S_even + S_odd + 1 = I_0(2√80). Gauss's figures give ≈ 5580212.7.
- S_even + 1 − S_odd = J_0(2√80).
- The column 2 and column 4 totals give √80·I_1(2√80) as their sum and the alternating Σ(−1)^k k t_k = −√80·J_1(2√80)·(−1)… i.e. x·d/dx J_0(2√x) evaluated at 80, as their difference.

PURPOSE (my inference, not stated). Splitting by parity suggests he wanted the alternating (Bessel J_0-type) value and its derivative. Note that 2√80 = 17.889 lies near the sixth zero of J_0 (18.071), so a Newton-type step or a cancellation test is plausible. Any purpose beyond evaluating these series is unsure.

His figures give 1 + S_e − S_o ≈ 33.2 and a weighted difference ≈ 404. The true values are ≈ −0.034 and ≈ +1.66. So the alternating results are swamped by the slips listed under errors. The next page restarts the computation with t10 = 815407.4148 (= 0.8 × his t9), i.e. a recomputation.
errors: t9: 80·t8/81 = 1019257.2685, but column 3 has 1019259.2685 (+2). His own 9t9 = 9173315.4167 in column 2 is correct. The column-3 total includes the wrong value.

t10: correct is 80^10/(10!)^2 = 815405.8148 (10t10 = 8154058.148). Gauss used 10t10 = 8154505.6148 (boxed), i.e. t10 = 815450.5615. This is a relative error of 5.5e-5, and it propagates into every later term of both chains.

t19: from 4t18/19 = 92.5268866 he multiplied by 18 instead of 20. This gave 19t19 = 1665.4840 and t19 = 87.6571 instead of 1850.54 and 97.3967. Hence t20 = 17.5314 (should be 19.479 relative to his t18), and the later even and odd terms are scaled down accordingly.
Column 4 addition: the sum to 11.5647 is 24247841.9960, but he wrote 24247842.0060 (+0.01).
Column 2 final: 24247436.3584 + 1.8284 + .0353 + .0005 = 24247438.2226, but the page shows ...2206 (−0.002, possibly a reading issue).

Consequence: the alternating combinations (≈33.2 and ≈404) are not the true J_0(2√80) ≈ −0.034 or the true derivative quantity ≈ 1.66. The plain total for I_0(2√80) is off only in the 5th–6th significant figure.

results.what: Numerical evaluation of Σ 80^k/(k!)^2 and Σ k·80^k/(k!)^2, split into even and odd parts, using the recurrences t_k = x t_{k-1}/k^2 and k t_k = x t_{k-1}/k
results.modern_name: Power-series evaluation of modified/ordinary Bessel functions I_0(2√x), J_0(2√x) (the confluent 0F1(;1;±x)) and their derivatives
results.usually_credited_to: Series known from Euler and Bernoulli (18th c.); Bessel functions systematised by Bessel (1824); 0F1 within Gauss's own 1812 hypergeometric work

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine numerical work: series terms by recurrence, then summed. Gauss is well known to have computed with 0F1/hypergeometric series. Splitting by parity, perhaps to get J_0 near a zero, is mildly interesting, but the work contains no new method and the alternating results are spoiled by arithmetic slips.

checkable.asserts: The alternating sum 1 + S_even − S_odd should be ≈ −0.034, not Gauss's ≈ 33.2
The true even-minus-odd weighted sum ≈ 1.66 (= −√80·J_1(2√80)); Gauss's columns give ≈ 404
The column 1 partial sum is 2425838.6693, one less than written
The column 3 partial sum is 2625856.3009, as written
